assertions.description: window.subApps is exposed exactly when the page is an isolated-app:// context: present inside an installed IWA, absent in any normal tab. This assertion is context-aware and passes in both places only when the gate behaves per the [IsolatedContext] IDL attribute.
The early experimental navigator.subApps surface is gone — the API ships on Window only. navigator must not carry a subApps attribute in any context.
The interface is [SecureContext]: on a non-secure context window.subApps must be absent.
Inside an installed IWA, window.subApps exposes add, remove, and list as functions returning promises.
assertions.test: Requires an installed Isolated Web App: open its window and verify typeof window.subApps.add / .remove / .list are all 'function'.

assertions.description: Under the AskSubApps default (DefaultSubAppsWithoutPromptsSetting = 3 or unset), declining the batch installation prompt rejects the whole add() promise with NotAllowedError.
assertions.test: Requires an installed IWA and a user declining the prompt: call window.subApps.add(['/some-subapp/']) and dismiss the confirmation dialog; the promise must reject with a DOMException named NotAllowedError.

assertions.description: With the origin listed in SubAppsWithoutPromptsAllowedForOrigins (or DefaultSubAppsWithoutPromptsSetting = 1), add() proceeds without any user prompt; with SubAppsWithoutPromptsBlockedForOrigins listed, the prompt is always required. Blocked overrides Allowed overrides Default.
assertions.test: Requires a managed ChromeOS profile: configure the three policies per the planner demo and verify the prompt appears exactly when the computed verdict says it should.

assertions.description: Individual sub-app failures (ConstraintError scope overlap, DataError invalid manifest, InvalidStateError already installed) surface per-path in SubAppsAddResponse.failedApps, not as batch rejections.
assertions.test: Requires an installed IWA: call add() with one valid and one invalid path and verify the response resolves with the valid path in installedApps and the invalid one mapped to a DOMException in failedApps.
